DNA is eluted with a small volume of water or loading dye containing formamide. The entire DNA purification procedure typically takes about 2 minutes.

DESCRIPTION: Aladdin's UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Loading Buffer (6X, Red) is used for loading DNA samples onto agarose or polyacrylamide gels for electrophoresis. It contains NA-Red (Nucleic Acid Red) fluorescent dye that binds to nucleic acids at the moment of mixing and emits red fluorescence under UV light.This product is easy to use. A simple three-step procedure includes adding 1/6 volume of 6X DNA Loading Buffer to DNA, loading onto gel and electrophoresis. There is no need to add any dye in agarose gels or stain gels after electrophoresis.This product is safe, sensitive, and highly stable. NA-Red is a significantly safer alternative to ethidium bromide, with very low mutagenicity and no cytotoxicity. It allows the detection of ＞0.6ng of DNA, and has good thermal and photo-stability. Please refer to Figure 1 for the sensitivity of this product.Figure 1. Image of different amounts of DNA loaded with Aladdin's UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Loading Buffer (6X, Red) on agarose gel after electrophoresis. The actual results may vary due to differences in DNA quality and detection instrument used.Imaging System documented with the same filters as ethidium bromide can be used. Red fluorescence is detected at a wavelength of about 300nm, which is very close to the excitation and emission light of EB.This product uses Red as an indicator for easy visual tracking of DNA migration during electrophoresis. Red comigrates with 20-50 bp DNA fragments, which usually does not interfere with the observation of DNA fragments.UltraBio™™ Red Fluorescent DNA Ladders should be used in parallel with this product. You can also use the regular DNA ladder supplemented with an appropriate amount of Aladdin's UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Marker dye (50X). Please refer to Figure 2 for the stain result of DNA samples loaded with this product and the UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Ladder .Figure 2. Image of the UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Ladder and DNA samples in different lengths loaded with Aladdin's UltraBio™ Red Fluorescent DNA Loading Buffer (6X, Red) on agarose gel after electrophoresis.Precautions：This product should be kept in the dark. Exposure to regular indoor light during the electrophoresis does not cause any change in its performance.This product can be added directly to DNA samples for loading and electrophoresis. Agarose gels after electrophoresis are not recommended for reuse.The gel can be observed directly after electrophoresis using a gel imager. If the background is too high, the gel can be washed with nuclease-free water to reduce the background.This product can stain dsDNA, ssDNA, and RNA.When smear or unsatisfactory band separation is observed, the following methods can be attempted: use freshly prepared electrophoresis buffer; reduce the loading amount of DNA; reduce the agarose concentration; use a longer gel; decrease the voltage for electrophoresis and extend the time of electrophoresis to improve DNA separation, etc.This product is compatible with commonly used electrophoresis buffers, such as TAE and TBE.This product is for R&D only. Not for drug, household, or other uses.For your safety and health, please wear a lab coat and disposable gloves during the operation.Instructions for Use：1. Prepare agarose gel with an appropriate concentration. Do not add any dye to the gel.2. Mix the 6X DNA Loading Buffer well before use. Add 1/6 volume of 6X DNA Loading Buffer to your DNA sample, mix well and load directly onto agarose gel for electrophoresis. Note: InstantView™ Red Fluorescent DNA Ladders (, D0115/D0117/D0120/D0122) should be used in parallel with this product.3. After electrophoresis, use a Gel Imager System for observation or taking photos.   Specification: 6X, Red

DESCRIPTION: Application  Ethidium bromide (EtBr) is the most commonly used nucleic acid stain for PAGE or agarose gel electrophoresis. DESCRIPTION: NRAS was discovered by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research, funded by the Cancer Research Campaign (now Cancer Research UK). NRAS gene is a member of the Ras gene family. It is mapped on chromosome 1, and it is activated in HL6, a promyelocytic leukemia line. The mammalian ras gene family consists of the Harvey and Kirsten ras genes (HRAS and KRAS), an inactive pseudogene of each (c-Hras2 and c-Kras1), and the N-ras gene. They differ significantly only in the C-terminal 4 amino acids. These ras genes have GTP/GDP binding and GTPase activity, and their normal function may be as G-like regulatory proteins involved in the normal control of cell growth. The NRAS gene specifies two main transcripts of 2Kb and 4.3Kb. The difference between the two transcripts is a simple extension through the termination site of the 2Kb transcript.
